index.title: A clearer path to a fair rent increase.
index.description: An evidence-first guide for two reported San Francisco tenancies. Understand the rules, protect privacy, and make a considered decision before giving notice.

sections.title: Executive summary
sections.intro: The annual rate is a starting point, not proof that a particular increase is lawful or typical.

cells: What is the current annual allowance?
1.6% of lawful base rent for ordinary annual increases effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027, subject to all other conditions.
Official rule
What is a considerate approach?

Consider no increase, or an ordinary-only adjustment at or below the applicable annual allowance after verifying each tenancy. Do not assume a catch-up amount. This is a recommendation, not a measured market norm.
Assessment
Does state law replace the local limit?
No. The separate AB 1482 figure applies to covered state-law units; it does not displace San Francisco’s more protective local rent regulations.
Official rule
What about a change in roommates?
Do not add rent solely because a roommate was added or assume a later agreement creates a vacancy. The tenancy and original-occupant status remain unverified.
Needs review
Raise one unit or both?
Use the same neutral decision criteria for each unit. Different eligibility dates or lease terms can matter; equal increases do not by themselves eliminate discrimination risk.
Assessment
Can a notice be served now?
No individualized amount or date is cleared here. Verify coverage, lawful base rent, notice history, license, lease terms, and any applicable restrictions; obtain legal review.
Not determined

cells: Local rent-control coverage
A building’s reported age alone does not establish coverage or resolve all exemptions.
Lawful monthly base rent
The annual allowance applies to base rent, excluding temporary passthroughs and fluctuating charges.
Original tenancy start / continuity
A later lease or occupancy change does not by itself prove a new vacant tenancy or anniversary.
Last lawful annual increase date
Ordinary annual and banked increases generally require at least 12 months after the last applicable increase.
Current lease term and increase clause
A fixed term may restrict a midterm increase even when the ordinance would otherwise allow one.
Available banked percentage
A complete rent and notice history is needed; do not assume any amount accrued.
Current increase license
The required Housing Inventory license must be effective before an annual or banked increase takes effect.
Lawful increase / effective date
Cannot be determined without the preceding facts, service requirements, and any additional restrictions.

rules.title: Know the limits before the numbers.
rules.description: San Francisco’s ordinary annual allowance is not the same as a market average or a license to increase rent. Other lawful components have separate rules.

sections.title: Ordinary increases and banking
sections.intro: Rules for an annual increase are distinct from separately permitted passthroughs and petitions.

cells: Eligibility
Many units built before June 14, 1979 may be covered, but exemptions and unit-specific facts matter.
Confirm official property records and classification; do not infer coverage from age alone.
Timing
The first ordinary increase may take effect at least 12 months after the tenancy begins; a subsequent annual increase generally follows the last applicable increase by at least 12 months.
A later effective date can establish a new anniversary; distinguish separately governed passthroughs.
Base rent
Calculate the annual increase on base rent, including applicable housing services but excluding temporary passthroughs and fluctuating charges. Do not round up to a whole dollar.
The owner-reported total must not be assumed to equal lawful base rent.
License
A current Housing Inventory rent increase license is needed for annual or banked increases by the effective date.
The license is necessary, not proof every other legal requirement is met.
A fully skipped increase
The Rent Board says a skipped increase is banked only if at least 24 full months pass without a rent increase; a later change of anniversary may lose an amount.
Do not infer a bank merely from a long lease.
Partially used increase
The unused portion of an allowable annual increase may be banked and imposed later under the Rent Board’s timing rules.
A smaller increase is permissible; check the remaining amount with the actual history.
Calculation
Eligible banked percentages are added, then applied to current base rent; the Rent Board says not to compound or prorate them.
Neither unit’s eligible bank or calculation is established here.
Other increases
Certain capital, operating-and-maintenance, and other increases have separate petition, worksheet, certification or notice requirements.
An expense or market-rent gap is not automatic permission to add a charge.

sections.title: Which laws apply?
sections.intro: Subsidies, a lease, or other laws may add protections. Coverage for these particular units is unverified.

cells: San Francisco
The ordinary annual allowance is 1.6% in the stated period for units subject to local rent-increase limits.
Not a universal ceiling on properly authorized banked or petition-based amounts.
California
For units subject to AB 1482, San Francisco’s state-law figure is 8.8% from Aug 1, 2026 through Jul 31, 2027.
This does not replace the local limit for units subject to it; applicable exemptions and dates matter.
Federal
The Fair Housing Act prohibits discrimination on protected grounds; federal housing assistance may have additional restrictions.
No federal program status or unit-specific federal numerical cap has been established here.

notice.title: Communicate clearly. Serve correctly.
notice.description: A friendly explanation is useful, but a letter, calculation and service must satisfy the applicable law and lease. This page is not an issued notice.

sections.title: Written notice and timing
sections.intro: These minimums generally apply to covered periodic tenancies; exceptions or a longer lease, program, or statutory requirement can change the result.

cells: Personal delivery; increase at or below 10%
At least 30 days
Measure the proposed increase together with increases in the prior 12 months under Civil Code § 827.
Personal delivery; increase above 10%
At least 90 days
The statute includes an income/family recertification exception and other laws may require more notice.
Mail within California; at or below 10%
At least 35 days
The ordinary California-mail extension adds five calendar days; confirm service requirements and any longer notice.
Mail within California; above 10%
At least 95 days
Mailing or delivery outside California, address-confidentiality programs, and special rules may require a different extension.
Fixed-term agreement
A midterm increase generally requires the agreement to expressly permit it. The current contracts have not been reviewed.
Notice components
Annual and banked portions, if any, must be identified in writing; the Board says to include the dollar increase, percentage and effective date.
Separate cost-based charges may need additional explanations and Board forms.

sections.title: A careful process
sections.intro: These are recommended steps, not a claim that they were completed.

cells: 01 · Verify
Privately confirm coverage, lease terms, lawful base rent, prior effective dates, Housing Inventory license, and any subsidy requirements.
The public website has no official property or lease records.
02 · Calculate
Choose a documented, neutral policy. For an ordinary 1.6% increase during the current period, multiply verified base rent by 0.016.
Do not round up or silently add a banked amount; apply the rate in effect on the increase date.
03 · Review
Check fair housing, retaliation, serious outstanding habitability conditions, and the wording and method of service with qualified counsel.
An owner’s explanation is not a substitute for statutory compliance or independent legal review.
04 · Inform
Give each affected tenant a properly served written notice that identifies the components, amount, percentage, and effective date; retain a copy and proof of service.
Keep ordinary annual increases separate from any special petition or passthrough.
05 · Invite questions
Provide a contact and direct tenants to Rent Board counseling and the tenant-petition process.
The Rent Board offers free information; counseling is not a lawyer’s individualized advice.

sections.title: Reasons: useful, but not shortcuts
sections.intro: A reason should be truthful and should identify the legal category; it does not create authority to charge an otherwise impermissible amount.

cells: Ordinary annual adjustment
A modest annual adjustment to support ongoing operation can be a transparent business explanation if true.
Identify the annual component and satisfy timing, license, lease and notice rules.
Maintenance or capital costs
Some costs may be eligible for a separately governed petition or passthrough.
Do not simply add a repair, tax, insurance, or improvement bill to base rent.
Nearby market rents are higher
A market difference by itself does not justify a special-circumstances comparables increase.
The Rent Board requires proof of qualifying extraordinary circumstances and comparable rents.
Additional occupant
An increase solely because an occupant was added to an existing tenancy is generally prohibited.
Narrow statutory exceptions and any petition must be analyzed independently.

fairness.title: Fairness is more than matching numbers.
fairness.description: An increase to one unit is not automatically discriminatory, and increasing both does not guarantee protection from a complaint. Apply and document neutral criteria, and seek professional review.

sections.title: The fair-housing review
sections.intro: These are safeguards and questions for an attorney, not a finding about either tenancy.

cells: One unit or both?
The laws focus on prohibited discrimination and retaliation; the sources do not establish a rule that every unit must receive the same increase.
Evaluate each unit’s lawful eligibility and document any neutral difference. Do not select a unit based on protected characteristics.
Same percentage?
A consistent policy can be easier to explain, but the same percentage does not cure an unlawful timing, lease, license, or discrimination problem.
Check each tenancy independently; avoid treating consistency as a legal safe harbor.
Protected characteristics
California protects characteristics including race, disability, familial status and source of income; federal law has its own protected categories.
Do not base pricing or treatment on protected characteristics or assumptions about them.
Retaliation
SF and California prohibit rent increases motivated by retaliation for protected exercise of rights, under their applicable standards.
Do not target a tenant for requesting repairs, organizing or asserting legal rights.
Repairs and habitability
California Civil Code § 1942.4 can bar a rent-increase notice when all specified serious-habitability conditions exist.
Review inspection and repair history; do not assume that every defect triggers the statute or that none exist.
Accommodations
California fair-housing law requires reasonable disability accommodations where applicable.
Consider a timely, individualized request and obtain legal advice where needed.
Legal clearance
No lawyer, advocate, Rent Board judge, or tenant has reviewed or approved the proposed action in this project.

sections.intro: These resources are provided by the City. Availability and eligibility can vary.

Rent Board tenant petition
Eligible tenants in locally rent-controlled units
A tenant can challenge an alleged unlawful increase or request review of lawful rent; the Board says filing is free.

practice.kicker: WHAT THE EVIDENCE CAN — AND CANNOT — SAY
practice.title: Big owners, small owners, same safeguards.
practice.description: The public evidence does not establish a typical San Francisco percentage by landlord size. An observed practice or a legal maximum is not a recommended target.

sections.title: What is actually documented?
sections.intro: National evidence is context, not a representative survey of the Outer Sunset or of these units.

cells: Institutional owners
GAO reviewed research on institutional investment in single-family housing and reported limited evidence about effects on tenants.
Do not treat national investment research as a local rent-increase average or a finding about every corporation.
Commercial pricing systems
In 2025 DOJ described allegations involving competitor data and a proposed settlement concerning a commercial rent-pricing provider.
These were allegations and a proposed settlement in that source, not proof of the conduct of all corporate landlords.
San Francisco pricing software
City law prohibits use or sale of the specifically defined algorithmic device that uses non-public competitor data to advise rents or occupancy.
The prohibition is not a ban on all algorithms or ordinary arithmetic.
Typical corporate increase in SF
No official, comparable citywide statistic was verified for this snapshot; do not substitute the annual allowance.
Typical individual-owner increase in SF
No official, comparable citywide statistic was verified for this snapshot; individual owners have no separate numerical allowance merely because they are small.
A policy for both units
Consider a predictable ordinary-only adjustment, or no increase, using the same neutral criteria and each unit’s legal timing.
This is a proposed practice, not an official market norm or a guarantee against claims.
